$comment: Advisories the CI security gate is allowed to ignore. See scripts/audit-gate.mjs.
An entry belongs here ONLY when there is no published fix to upgrade or
override to, AND the vulnerable code path is unreachable from this app.
If a patched version exists, pin it via `overrides` in package.json instead —
Every entry needs an `expires` date. On that date the gate starts failing
again, forcing a re-evaluation. That is deliberate: this file must not become
a place where advisories go to be forgotten.

allow.title: image-size: ICNS parser allows denial of service through an infinite loop
reason: No published fix exists. The advisory's vulnerable range is `<= 2.0.2`
and 2.0.2 IS the latest published version (April 2025); the GitHub
advisory record carries no first_patched_version at all. There is
nothing to upgrade to and nothing to pin via `overrides`. npm's
`fixAvailable` proposes downgrading expo 57 to 53, which is a two-major
downgrade of the whole mobile app and does not even remove image-size.
Reachability: image-size is a transitive dependency of metro (the React
Native bundler) via expo — `metro/src/Assets.js` imports it to read the
dimensions of image assets at bundle time. It parses files that are in
this repository, on a developer machine or an EAS builder; it never sees
user-supplied input, and it ships in no runtime artifact — not the server
bundle, not the web bundle, not the app binary. A malformed ICNS would
hang our own build, not a user.
Review on expiry: we resolve image-size 1.2.1, via metro's `^1.0.2` —
so a fix published as 2.0.3 would NOT arrive by upgrade, and forcing
2.x through `overrides` hands metro a major bump of its image parser.
What clears this is a 1.x backport, metro widening its range, or metro
moving off the package. Check for those; otherwise re-confirm the
build-time-only assumption above still holds and extend.

allow.title: image-size: JXL and HEIF parsers allow denial of service through infinite loops
reason: Same package, same range (`<= 2.0.2`), same absent fix and same
build-time-only reachability as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr above — see that
entry. Different parsers (JXL/HEIF rather than ICNS), so npm reports it
as a second advisory and the gate needs it named separately.
Review both entries together on expiry: one image-size release clears
them at once.
